candidates.attacker_control: The multipart part header `Content-Disposition: form-data; name=...; filename="<payload>"` (surfaced by the streaming parser as `FileItemStream.getName()`), plus the request `Content-Length` used to exceed `struts.multipart.maxSize` (default 2097152, `core/src/main/resources/org/apache/struts2/default.properties:72`). In the sibling default-parser paths the multipart `Content-Type`/parser error text is the attacker-influenced text (the publicly exploited S2-045 vector). No authentication is assumed beyond access to the multipart endpoint.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Confirmed in source that (a) `addFileSkippedError` is the only caller that places a client-supplied filename into an exception message used for localization (private method, called only at line 299); (b) that path is gated solely on request size (`isRequestSizePermitted`, 319-328; `maxSize` injected from `struts.multipart.maxSize`, 76-79), which the attacker controls via `Content-Length`; (c) the misspelled singular key prefix guarantees the default-message fall-back (bundle has plural keys only, `struts-messages.properties:35-36`); (d) `findText(Class, key, locale, defaultMessage, args)` obtains a live value stack from `ActionContext` (391-395) and `getDefaultMessage` translates the default message (729); (e) `translateVariables` treats `$` and `%` as expression openers (TextParseUtil:46-47). Considered mitigation: evaluation passes through `SecurityMemberAccess` (excluded classes/packages, `struts.ognl.allowStaticMethodAccess=false`), which genuinely restricts payloads and is the main reason I rate this medium-confidence; also considered that the default parser is `jakarta`, so the filename path needs the streaming parser and the sibling paths depend on third-party (commons-fileupload/container) exception text that is not present in the snapshot.
candidates.impact: Framework compiles and evaluates attacker-supplied text as an OGNL expression against the live request value stack (expression/code injection). In the documented exploitation of this exact multipart error-message path (CVE-2017-5638 / S2-045–S2-046) this led to remote code execution and full application compromise; even where the expression sandbox blocks a given payload, untrusted data is still interpreted as code and the evaluated result is surfaced to the user, making the finding a high-severity injection primitive.
candidates.prerequisites: Application maps a multipart-capable endpoint (e.g. `fileUpload` interceptor / any multipart POST). For the fully in-repo filename path the streaming parser must be selected (`struts.multipart.parser=jakarta-stream`; the default is `jakarta`, and the `jakarta-stream` bean is registered at `core/src/main/resources/struts-default.xml:92-93`), and the request must pass the size check (`Content-Length >= struts.multipart.maxSize`) or otherwise raise a parser error; `requestSizePermitted` is false then, so `addFileSkippedError(itemStream.getName(), request)` runs. Expression evaluation is subject to `SecurityMemberAccess` (excluded classes/packages, static access off) — a sandbox that historically did not prevent exploitation of this same error-message path.
candidates.root_cause: Multipart error handling passes attacker-influenced exception text as the `defaultMessage` argument of `LocalizedTextUtil.findText(...)`, and `LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage()` unconditionally runs that default message through `TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack)`, which evaluates every `${...}`/`%{...}` fragment as an OGNL expression on the request value stack. In `JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest`, `addFileSkippedError()` embeds the client-supplied multipart filename in a `FileSizeLimitExceededException` message (`"Skipped file " + fileName + "; request size limit exceeded."`), and `buildErrorMessage()` passes that message as the default message; the lookup key is also never resolved (`struts.message.upload.error.` — singular — while the bundle defines `struts.messages.upload.error.*` only, and no `FileSizeLimitExceededException` entry exists), so untrusted text is always the string that gets OGNL-evaluated. `JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage()` and `MultiPartRequestWrapper.buildErrorMessage()` contain the same `e.getMessage()`-as-default-message pattern (same root cause, default-parser paths).
candidates.title: Attacker-controlled multipart error text (filename) is evaluated as an OGNL expression via LocalizedTextUtil default-message translation
candidates.trace: HTTP multipart POST → `JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest.parse()` (236-247) → `processUpload()` (266-311) → `ServletFileUpload.getItemIterator(request)` → `itemStream.getName()` = attacker filename → `addFileSkippedError(itemStream.getName(), request)` (299) → exception message `"Skipped file " + fileName + "; request size limit exceeded."` (350) → `buildErrorMessage(exception, args)` (352 → 510-514) → `LocalizedTextUtil.findText(Class, "struts.message.upload.error.FileSizeLimitExceededException", locale, <filename-bearing message>, args)` (513) → `ActionContext.getContext().getValueStack()` (392) → bundle lookup fails (only plural `struts.messages.upload.error.SizeLimitExceededException`/`IOException` exist, `core/src/main/resources/org/apache/struts2/struts-messages.properties:35-36`) → `getDefaultMessage(...)` (573/714-737) → `TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack)` (729) → `OgnlTextParser`/`ValueStack.findValue(<payload>)` → OGNL evaluation of the attacker text in the current action's value stack, and the resulting string is stored in `errors`/action errors and rendered.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed: no build, execution, or payload was run (per instructions), and the snapshot contains no `src/test/**` tree, so intended behavior could not be checked against tests. Whether the `SecurityMemberAccess` sandbox is bypassable for this snapshot's exact configuration was not verified. For the default `jakarta` parser, the exception text that embeds attacker input is produced by commons-fileupload/servlet-container code outside this snapshot, so only the Struts-side handling (untrusted text used as a variable-translated default message) is verified.
candidates.weakness_type: Expression language / OGNL injection leading to remote code execution (CWE-917, CWE-94); unsafe use of untrusted text as the default i18n message that is variable-translated

coverage_summary: Source scope: 2,643 readable files (core, plugins, apps, archetypes, bundles, assembly, poms; 0 files excluded for size/symlink/sensitive-name, binary-like files skipped by the reader/search when a NUL byte appears in the first 8 KiB). P1 relation index: status complete, all 2,643 source files indexed (0 missing, 0 hash mismatches), 17,284 symbols, 36,023 call rows, 34,339 edges, 453 facts; the index is explicitly syntactic/navigation-only (no data flow, no reachability, no SAST oracle or findings), so every relation I used was verified against the source text. I inspected with source reads: core dispatcher/filter/Prepare-Execute operations, action mappers (`DefaultActionMapper`, `Restful(2)ActionMapper`, `PrefixBasedActionMapper`), `DefaultActionProxy`/`DefaultActionInvocation`/`AllowedMethods`/`ActionConfig`/`XmlConfigurationProvider`/`DefaultConfiguration` (DMI/SMI chain), OGNL stack (`OgnlUtil`, `OgnlValueStack`, `SecurityMemberAccess`, accessors), interceptor security (`ParametersInterceptor`, `CookieInterceptor`, `FileUploadInterceptor`, `DebuggingInterceptor`, `StaticParametersInterceptor`), pattern checkers (`DefaultExcludedPatternsChecker`, `DefaultAcceptedPatternsChecker`), `LocalizedTextUtil`/`TextParseUtil`/`OgnlTextParser`/`PropertiesReader`, results (`ServletRedirectResult`, `ServletActionRedirectResult`, `StreamResult`, `XSLTResult`), `DefaultStaticContentLoader`, `RequestUtils`, multipart package (all three parsers + wrapper), `plugins/rest` (mapper, invocation, proxy factory, handlers, `struts-plugin.xml`), `plugins/json` (interceptor, populator), `plugins/sitegraph`, `plugins/convention` action-config builder, and sampled `apps/showcase`. Not inspected in depth (only listed/skimmed): `plugins/embeddedjsp` bundled Jasper tree (hundreds of files), velocity/freemarker/sitemesh/javatemplates template engines and JSP tag classes, portlet/OSGi/CDI/Spring/JasperReports/JFreeChart/GXP/DWR/OVal plugins, and most non-Java web assets; no index record was treated as evidence about those areas.
limitations: No build, execution, unit tests, scanners, or exploit payloads were run (read-only review); the candidate is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
The snapshot contains no `src/test/**` sources (only a few test-support classes under `src/main/java`), so I could not use tests to confirm intended semantics of the checks or to validate behavior.

No VCS metadata/diff data is present, so 'deviation from upstream' judgements rest on internal consistency and source reasoning rather than on a patch comparison; I could not verify which security fix a later commit would have applied.

The default multipart parser is `jakarta`; the fully in-repo filename path requires `struts.multipart.parser=jakarta-stream`, so runtime reachability depends on deployment configuration that cannot be observed here.

Effectiveness of the OGNL sandbox (`SecurityMemberAccess`, excluded classes/packages, disabled static access) against a full payload was not verified; this is the main reason the candidate is rated medium confidence.
The relation index proves nothing about runtime behavior or exploitability (no control/data-flow, no reachability, no scanner findings); areas without index records were not assumed reviewed.

Third-party dependencies (commons-fileupload, OGNL, XStream, servlet containers) are not part of the snapshot, so behavior attributed to them (e.g. which exception messages embed attacker input) is unverifiable here.

rejected_leads.lead: REST plugin XStream deserialization: `plugins/rest/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/rest/handler/XStreamHandler.java:48-50` builds a plain `new XStream()` (and `toObject` calls `fromXML` on the request body) with no type restrictions — the historical CVE-2017-9805/S2-052 pattern.
rejected_leads.reason: Real design weakness but it is this era's intended upstream default and requires the REST plugin plus the `application/xml` handler to be reachable; I could not tie it to a fix/config change in the snapshot, and it is a different root cause from the selected candidate, so it is kept only as an unconfirmed lead (not counted as a candidate).

rejected_leads.lead: `SecurityMemberAccess.isClassExcluded()` uses `clazz.isAssignableFrom(excludedClass)` (core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/ognl/SecurityMemberAccess.java:144-154), which does not block subclasses of listed classes such as `java.lang.ClassLoader`/`ProcessBuilder`.
rejected_leads.reason: Could not establish that this is a deviation from upstream rather than long-standing design: `java.lang.Object` is in `struts.excludedClasses` (core/src/main/resources/struts-default.xml:41-56), so the 'natural' direction would exclude every class and break all OGNL access; the same inverted-looking idiom also appears in unrelated upstream conversion classes. No source-level proof of exploitability (and no test sources to confirm intent), so not submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: `DefaultActionMapper.allowedActionNames` default regex (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/mapper/DefaultActionMapper.java:123) — `^[a-zA-Z0-9_!/\\-]*((.htm[l]?)|(.action))?$` — differs from the pattern shape I associate with upstream and uses an unescaped dot in the optional trailing group.
rejected_leads.reason: Analysis of the pattern shows it is stricter than a `[a-zA-Z0-9._!/\-]*` default (dots in the middle of action names are rejected) and the only unintended tolerance is for characters immediately preceding `htm`/`html`/`action`; I found no way to turn this into traversal, namespace or OGNL injection, so no concrete security impact could be substantiated.

rejected_leads.lead: `LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage()` translating the default message with `TextParseUtil.translateVariables` (core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/util/LocalizedTextUtil.java:729) as a standalone finding.
rejected_leads.reason: This is the sink of the submitted candidate's root cause; treating it separately would split one root cause into two candidates, so it is described inside the submitted candidate instead.

Verified in source: the showcase DAOs are in-memory storage wrappers with Spring `@Autowired` fields (the index's "injection" facts are dependency injection), and the sitegraph `exec` uses command-line arguments of a developer tool, not HTTP input — neither is attacker-controlled.

rejected_leads.lead: `FileUploadInterceptor.hasAllowedExtension()` accepting any filename ending in an allowed extension (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/interceptor/FileUploadInterceptor.java:388-401) and `XWorkBasicConverter.doConvertToClass()` calling `Class.forName` on request values (core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/conversion/impl/XWorkBasicConverter.java:164-170).
rejected_leads.reason: Both match the code that ships in this Struts generation (defaults are permissive by design: no `allowedExtensions`/`allowedTypes` configured means any file is accepted, and `Class`-typed properties are not used by default stacks); I could not show a snapshot-specific deviation or a reachable attacker path with impact, so they are recorded as unconfirmed leads.

summary: Reviewed the Struts 2.5.1-SNAPSHOT tree (2,643 readable files; core dispatcher/mapper/multipart/interceptor/OGNL paths, REST and JSON plugins, plus sampled app code after the P1 relation index — 2,643 indexed files / 17,284 symbols / 36,023 calls / 34,339 edges, navigation-only, no SAST findings). Testing first-layer "hardening" code (SMI allowed-methods, action-name allowlist, parameter/cookie excluded+accepted pattern checkers, SecurityMemberAccess, static-content loader, redirect result) showed those guards are present and internally consistent, so I traced the strongest remaining untrusted-input → dangerous-sink path: multipart error text is fed as the *default* i18n message and is therefore compiled and evaluated as OGNL against the request value stack. The most concrete, fully in-repo instance is the multipart filename in `JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest.addFileSkippedError()` → `buildErrorMessage()` → `LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage()` → `TextParseUtil.translateVariables()`. I submit that as the single candidate; other leads (XStream default in the REST plugin, reversed `isAssignableFrom` in `SecurityMemberAccess`, the `allowedActionNames` regex) are listed as rejected/unconfirmed leads rather than additional candidates. No code was executed, no tests exist in the snapshot, and no finding here is runtime-confirmed.
